summary.headline: LAPL Automotive H1 FY27 revenue rose 4% to INR43.64 crores while EBITDA margin fell to 14.42% from 15.29%, with growth guided to H2.
summary.overview: Inaugural earnings call after the BSE SME listing on August 13, 2026, covering H1 FY27 (half year ended September 30, 2026). Revenue from operations grew 4% YoY to INR43.64 crores, while EBITDA was flat at INR6.33 crores and net profit fell to INR2.97 crores from INR3.3 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to higher raw material share, added headcount, and higher depreciation and finance cost from capacity investment. Growth is expected to come from new programs and machinery arriving in H2, with a fourth plant targeted in about 8 months.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR6.41 crores in H1 FY26
vs INR3.3 crores in H1 FY26; net margin 6.76%

financial_highlights.value: INR15.45 crores (long-term about INR2.10 crores; balance working capital CC)

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Management cited gross margin of about 30%, the highest of the three segments. The new plant will be entirely dedicated to lighting, including LED, projector and adaptive headlamps, and an in-house tool room.

segments.name: Motors
segments.commentary: Management cited gross margin of about 20% (stated as 18-20%). Three new vendor codes were added, with motors new to these customers; the target is about 50,000 motors a year from the three new customers against 15,000 per month for existing customers.

segments.name: Mirrors
segments.commentary: Management cited gross margin of about 20%. Mirror order book reached 75,000 units this month, up from 15,000-20,000 units when mirror production started; BGAUSS rear-view mirror production starts October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management expects about 40% growth in FY27 on a conservative basis, implying roughly INR130 crores for the full year and about INR80-90 crores in H2.
Indent of about INR15 crores per month planned for H2 FY27.
EBITDA margin for H2 targeted at 14.5% to 15.5%, with a stated aim to bring margins back toward FY26 levels once volumes catch up.
Management sees a drastic jump of about 80% and 120% growth in coming years once the fourth plant's core unit is up.
Fourth plant expected to start in about 8 months (shed about 4 months, machinery about 3 months, setup about 1 month).
capex_capacity: Lighting and motor divisions ran at about 91% utilization in FY26; management says they are currently at full capacity.
Fourth manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: Bhumi Pujan on August 19, 2026, construction started in September-October 2026.
Space is about eight times the smallest existing unit; the plant will add about 14 molding machines of higher tonnage to the existing 14 machines (80-200 tons).

Remaining IPO proceeds of INR19.56 crores are earmarked for the new plant; advance paid to the builder and machinery to be ordered once the shed is ready. Of the INR32.4 crore IPO, about INR4.8 crores went to loan repayment, INR3.25 crores to IPO expenses and about INR4.8 crores to general corporate purposes.
Machinery is being added in steps; a new winding machine has been ordered for a motor product in development, while other processes run on existing lines.
demand_pricing: Revenue shortfall attributed to vendor-code onboarding; new programs typically contribute from H2. Lighting R&D cycles run 6-12 months; 19-20 R&D products are in progress.
Mirror order book at 75,000 units this month, versus 15,000-20,000 units when production started.

Plastic molded parts currently priced at INR20-80 each; new plant products expected at INR200-250, rising to INR800 for bumpers and dashboards. Management says margin in percentage terms stays the same but value per product rises.
LED and projector headlamps for buses average about INR2,000 per unit; bus headlamp ticket size rises to about INR16,000 per bus from INR3,000-4,000.
Customer concentration: Varroc Engineering is the top customer, about 75% of revenue in FY26 (management's illustrative figure). Management says concentration should fall as new customers grow.
Pipeline: JSW Motor, JSW Green, Mahindra Logistics, Ather discussed; Toyota targeted as Tier 2 supplier. OEM customers were about 78% of FY26 revenue, own LAPL brand about 22%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue not keep pace with two- and four-wheeler sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 effort went into the listing and new vendor codes; new programs start contributing mainly in H2. Capacity at 91% limits extra volume until the new plant is ready.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Lighting about 30% gross margin; motors and mirrors about 20% each.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise from FY23 to FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product value addition, new machinery reducing bottlenecks, renegotiated supplier prices with new vendors, and ERP implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Total borrowings INR15.45 crores at about 8.25%. Management said it will scale up borrowings, possibly through a higher CC limit, and is talking with other banks for better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Debtor and inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose on H2 raw material purchases. Debtors rose from August-September invoicing; average recovery is about 45 days. Working capital days are about 50-60.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in 40% H2-weighted growth?
qa_highlights.answer: A customer-side delay pushed a promised order book into coming months; management says the order book is intact and H2 indent is about INR15 crores per month.

risks_watch: H1 growth of 4% against guided 40% full-year growth requires about INR80-90 crores in H2; watch monthly billing against the INR15 crore/month indent.
Margin dilution from depreciation, finance cost and headcount ahead of new revenue; H2 EBITDA guidance of 14.5-15.5% depends on volume ramp.
Customer concentration: Varroc is about 75% of FY26 revenue, and new customers have only three vendor codes with small initial volumes.
Debtor days rose to about 76 and inventory days to about 94 (from 26 and 60 in FY23), per an analyst's figures; management cites timing of H2 ramp-up.
Fourth plant timeline (about 8 months) and remaining INR19.56 crore IPO-funded capex; execution and cost overrun risk.
Management commentary was inconsistent on whether H1 would be good, which an investor questioned; the customer-side delay explanation was given only on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and new customers, but cautious and at times evasive on H1 shortfall and near-term numbers, which management tied to customer delays and capacity timing. Answers on debt and receivables were less precise, with several follow-ups needed.
key_quotes: To be transparent with you, profitability this half was lower than the last year.
We see these as investments in the next phase of growth, and we are focused on bringing margins back towards the level we delivered in FY26.
We are running at full capacity.
Once you get the vendor code, the PO and the indent and the sales come in.

adds.what: Fourth manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (dedicated to lighting, incl. LED, projector and adaptive headlamps, plus tool room; ~14 higher-tonna

growth.why: Management guides ~40% FY27 revenue growth (~INR130 cr, implying INR80-90 cr in H2 vs INR43.6 cr in H1), backed by a 3-vendor-code onboarding, a 75,000-unit mirror order book, a ~INR15 cr/month H2 indent and a fourth plant starting in ~8 months; the H2 step-up is large relative to H1 run-rate and the plant lands after most of FY27, so backing is partial.

quality.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew only 4% YoY to INR43.64 crores with no stated driver (volume, price or mix) and no one-offs identified in the brief; management attributes the shortfall to customer-side onboarding delays and says new programs contribute mainly from H2, so the growth quality cannot be confirmed from the facts given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H2 EBITDA margin guided to 14.5-15.5% vs H1 14.42%, with aim to return toward FY26's 16.75% once volumes catch up, though H1 margin fell from 15.29% on raw material mix, headcount and depreciation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fourth plant in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is under construction (started Sep-Oct 2026) and guided to start in about 8 months, with about 14 higher-tonnage molding machines added to the existing 14.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 40% FY27 growth (~INR130 cr), implying INR80-90 cr in H2 vs INR43.64 cr in H1, backed by a ~INR15 cr/month H2 indent and mirror order book of 75,000 units; H1 growth was only 4%, so the step-up is large.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Lighting and motor divisions ran at about 91% utilization in FY26 and are at full capacity now; the fourth plant is already funded from the INR19.56 cr remaining IPO proceeds, and further machinery is being added in steps.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew only 4% against the 40% FY27 guide, with a customer-side delay pushing an order book into coming months, so an upgrade looks improbable near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs INR80-90 cr (about double the H1 run-rate of INR43.64 cr), and the plant lands only in about 8 months; the 40% guide depends on the monthly INR15 cr indent converting into billing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mirror production for BGAUSS starts October 2026, three new motor vendor codes are onboarding, and 19-20 lighting R&D products are in progress with 6-12 month cycles, though fourth-plant products (INR200-250 per part, bus headlamps at about INR16,000 per bus) arrive later.

rows.label: New OEM customers and vendor codes (Tier 1 onboarding)
rows.why: Three new vendor codes added with motors new to those customers, targeting about 50,000 motors a year vs 15,000 per month from existing customers; pipeline includes JSW, Mahindra Logistics, Ather and Toyota (Tier 2).

rows.label: Working capital build ahead of H2 ramp
rows.why: Debtor days rose to about 76 and inventory days to about 94 (vs 26 and 60 in FY23), and borrowings are INR15.45 cr at about 8.25%, with management planning a higher CC limit to fund the ramp.

rows.label: Mirror order book conversion
rows.why: Mirror order book reached 75,000 units this month vs 15,000-20,000 units when production started, with BGAUSS rear-view mirror production starting October 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on medium-term growth, new customers and the fourth plant, but cautious and at times evasive on the H1 shortfall, tying it to customer delays and capacity timing; analysts pressed on the H2-weighted 40% guide, inconsistent H1 commentary, and rising debtor and inventory days.
